notes: Override of abstract NanoTimer.method446. Returns GameClock.method599(mode xor 0x71.inv()) (the adjusted wall-clock millisecond value, xor'd back to plain since GameClock.method599 itself xor's/guards its own arg) converted to nanoseconds (*1_000_000). This is the millisecond-clock-based fallback NanoTimer implementation, contrasted with SystemNanoTimer (Clock.nanos()) and NanoTimerHighPrecision. All real call sites (InterfaceComponentGroup.kt, SceneLoaderThread.kt) pass mode=1. Suspicious dead branch: `if (i != 1) method446(76)` recurses into itself with a literal 76 whenever called with any mode other than 1, discards the result, and then falls through to the normal return -- since 76 != 1, a mode!=1 call would recurse indefinitely (stack overflow); this path is never exercised by any known caller and looks like an obfuscator-injected opaque/decoy branch rather than real logic.
